note: Approximate heartland extents of the divided kingdoms — Israel (c. 930-722 BC) and Judah (c. 930-586 BC). Drawn as era-context highlighting for the battle catalogue, NOT surveyed boundaries: borders shifted continually (Ramah, Beth-shemesh, the Transjordan) and scholarly maps differ. Vertices follow the conventional atlas picture: Israel from the Jezreel/Carmel line and coastal Sharon edge up to Dan and across Gilead; Judah from the Bethel plateau south through the Shephelah edge and Negev to Beersheba, east to the Dead Sea.

properties.name: Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)
properties.detail: The northern kingdom of the ten tribes, from the schism under Jeroboam I to the fall of Samaria to Assyria in 722/721 BC. Capitals: Shechem, Tirzah, then Samaria. Approximate heartland including Galilee and Gilead.

properties.name: Kingdom of Judah
properties.detail: The southern kingdom of the house of David, from the schism to the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC. Capital: Jerusalem. Approximate heartland from the Benjamin plateau to Beersheba and the Dead Sea shore.
